title: The Ophan's demand: six questions
eyebrow: Design area: the demand loop · step 1 of 2 · nothing built

short.lead: Each of the six open questions about the Ophan's demand has two or three options here, with my suggestion marked and room for your own answer. Every option is a number or a switch in one data file, OphanDemandTuning. That way, if a first guess plays badly, you change the number in the Unity Inspector instead of the code. Some options come from the fear pass you approved on 2026-10-11 (docs/7-design/fear-pass.md, "The creature hunts you through time"), and they're marked as such.
short.hint: Tap a card for what's already settled or what one question decides. Every number is on the card "The numbers".
items: A raid lasts 5 minutes at most.
The first demand shows in the Lair before the first raid and is due at the end of it.
The first piece is deep in the vault, and the players are told so. You must be able to fail it.
The Ophan hunts in the last 60 seconds of a raid.
Caught carrying the piece, it takes the piece and you live. Caught empty-handed, you die.
From the fear pass: a piece carried home and placed in the Lair also pays the demand; the Lair and the Market are always safe.
Every number, with the default that matches my suggestions
RaidSeconds 300: how long a raid lasts.
HuntWindowSeconds 60: how long before the portal closes the Ophan arrives.
RaidsBetweenDemandsMin 3 and Max 5: set both to 1 for a demand every raid.
HuntEveryRaidWhileOwed on; SpoilsTakenWhileOwed 1.0: the share of a hunted raid's haul it takes (0.5 takes half).
UnscheduledVisitChance 0.0: the chance it comes when nothing is due.
HuntSecondsAfterPaid 0: 0 leaves at once, 300 hunts until the portal closes.
DemandsToConfront 12: paid demands before you can face it.
FirstPieceMinRoomsFromPortal 6: how deep "deep in the vault" is, in rooms.
Nothing from you. Your answers set the defaults.
1. How often a demand falls due
After the first demand, the next is due in 1 raid, in a fixed number of raids, or in a random number between two limits.
Death in that raid, and possibly something that carries over: every raid becomes a hunt until you pay, or the next demand gets bigger.
Only on raids where a demand is due or still owed, or on every raid, or mostly on due raids with a small chance on the others.
When it takes the piece, it either leaves at once or keeps hunting the empty-handed for a while. This is one number: how many seconds it keeps hunting after being paid.
5. What a paid demand gives you
A rung on a ladder toward facing it, one of its weaknesses revealed, or nothing directly, so that strength comes only from what you buy.
The ledger's sketch alone, or the sketch plus a faint mark on the piece when you are close. Both come with a setting for how close.

changes: OphanDemandTuning, one data file for the demand
Every number on this page in one asset, edited in the Inspector.

It follows the pattern of TrueFormTuning on the Wick branch: each number has a tooltip saying what it does. The fields and their defaults are on the In short card "The numbers". A test checks that every default loads and that no value is out of range.
The fear pass says the interval is configurable, but no tuning file exists yet.
One asset holding every number for the demand.
When a playtest feels wrong, you change a number, not the code.
choices: often
After the first demand, how often does one fall due?
A
A random number of raids between 3 and 5
This is the fear pass's rule. At 5 minutes a raid, that's a demand every 15 to 25 minutes. Fields: RaidsBetweenDemandsMin 3, Max 5.
B
Every raid
Every raid has a target, so pressure is constant. Fields: Min 1, Max 1.
C
A fixed number of raids, such as every 2
Easy to plan around. Fields: Min 2, Max 2.
Between demands, the in-between raids are free to spend on loot and upgrades. A range keeps the deadline from becoming a routine.
fail
What does failing a demand cost?
A
Every raid is a hunt until you pay, and it takes that raid's haul
This is the fear pass's rule. Fields: HuntEveryRaidWhileOwed on, SpoilsTakenWhileOwed 1.0, which can be eased to 0.5.
B
Death in that raid only; the demand is due again next raid
The mildest option. Fields: HuntEveryRaidWhileOwed on, SpoilsTakenWhileOwed 0.
C
The next demand gains an extra piece, up to a cap
The debt grows. Fields: ExtraPiecesPerMissedDemand 1, MaxPiecesPerDemand 3.
It's already approved, it hurts without wiping progress, and the share it takes can be softened with one number.
comes
When does the Ophan come?
A
Only when a demand is due or still owed
This is the fear pass's rule. Field: UnscheduledVisitChance 0.
B
On every raid, in the last 60 seconds
Every raid ends in a chase, even when nothing is due. Field: UnscheduledVisitChance 1.0.
C
When a demand is due, plus a small chance on other raids
There's a surprise now and then. Field: UnscheduledVisitChance 0.1.
Its visits stay meaningful, and the chance field is already there if you want surprises later.
holder
When it takes the piece, does that save everyone?
A
Yes, it leaves at once
Everyone protects the carrier. Field: HuntSecondsAfterPaid 0.
B
It keeps hunting the empty-handed for a short while
The others must still run. Field: HuntSecondsAfterPaid 15.
C
No, it hunts the empty-handed until the portal closes
Each player is on their own. Field: HuntSecondsAfterPaid 300.
The whole raid becomes about getting one piece to one person, which suits a co-op game. The number can be raised if that's too easy.
toward
What does a paid demand give you toward defeating it?
A
A rung on a visible ladder; after enough rungs you can face it
Field: DemandsToConfront 12. The rungs show in the ledger.
B
One of its weaknesses revealed, as a ledger page
You face it when you have the weaknesses and the gear to use them. Field: WeaknessesToReveal.
C
Nothing directly; strength comes only from what you buy
You choose when you feel strong enough.
It's the simplest to build and to tune, and progress is always visible. Option B can be added later on top.
recognise
How do players recognise the demanded piece?
A
The ledger's sketch, plus a faint mark on the piece when you are near
Fields: PieceMarkRadius 6 m, PieceMarkLastsForDemands 3, after which only the sketch is left.
B
The ledger's sketch only
Hardest; you must know it by sight. Field: PieceMarkRadius 0.
C
The mark is always on
The easiest. Field: PieceMarkLastsForDemands set very high.
Helps new players at first, then the help fades so recognising pieces becomes a skill.
